title: Transcription dates and cigarette advertising
summary: Commercial transcription work paid well, before residuals.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: A lot of people don't know what you're talking about
transcriptions but the point of this --

In those days it was radio commercials or TV commercials, the background music that you hear behind the advertisements on the air. And in those days there were a great many, particularly before cigarette advertising was banned, half the work everyone did was for cigarette advertising, because all the agencies would compete to get the accounts. So they were constantly having transcription dates, there were about 10 or 15 agencies, and each one was trying to get the different Chesterfield account, so you would do 15/ transcriptions for Chesterfield, and get paid the same whether you got the program or not. Because in those days they didn't have what they call residuals now. Now you get a repayment every 13 weeks, but that's only in the last 10 years.
But in the days when I did all my work, they didn't have those things, residuals.
Yeah, you were in on the beginning.
